thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: smart-routing policy mismatch detected for prod-service A. 5xx spike and elevated latency from us-east->us-west fallbacks. Root rule: policy 'route-by-cost-v2' returned incompatible model variant.

sara (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing context and logs. what's the customer impact?

support-bot: ~1200 requests/min failing 502 for customers on prod keys east-region since ~10s ago. Errors show model handshake timeout with 'redwood-13b-legacy' variant.

jordan: seeing continuous region fallback loop in the tracer: requests from us-east routed to us-west, then fallback to us-east pinned variant, repeat -> KV cache churn.

lee: quick note — this came after the routing policy rollout at 08:10. `route-by-cost-v2` added a variant pin step for high-priority customers. possible mis-tagging of variants.

sara (oncall): can we force routes away from the pinned variant to stop the loop? need mitigation now.

jordan: proposed short-term: `redwoodctl routes override --service prod-service --policy route=region-prefer --region us-east` to bypass variant pinning.

lia: heads up, forcing a region will drop to fallback model `redwood-13b-quant` which is compatible but uses more GPU mem on us-east. possible saturation.

sara (oncall): do it anyway. we prefer latency and stability over cost. executing now.

<sara ran command, bot message> ops-bot: Executing override: `redwoodctl override set --service prod-service --force-region us-east --bypass-variant true` (applied by sara).

support-bot: Traffic rerouted. error rate down from 14% -> 7% in 20s. some customers still seeing intermittent 502s.

maria (oncall): I'm taking the secondary pager. entering handoff. what's next?

sara (oncall): handing off — override applied, monitoring. If errors drop below 1% in 10m we keep this for stabilization. lia and jordan please investigate why the policy pinned incompatible variant.

lia: looking at policy config — there's a new rule matching customer tag `enterprise-v2` that pins `redwood-13b-legacy` when `latency_budget < 150ms`. That variant isn't present in us-east due to recent model pruning. So the router was forcing cross-region calls that then failed.

jordan: logs show a cascade: router tried us-east->us-west, us-west rejected due to full queue, routed back to us-east, router saw incompatible model hash and forced legacy, loop continued. hitting KV cache invalidation thrice per request.

maria (oncall): okay, mitigation seems to have reduced the immediate loop, but CPU/GPU in us-east spiked due to the `redwood-13b-quant` fallback. we're seeing saturation on a couple of dedicated pools.

sara (oncall): roll back override? that feels risky. any other short-term levers?

lia: we can roll back the policy rollout (revert `route-by-cost-v2`) but that will momentarily reintroduce older behavior. OR we can unpin the `enterprise-v2` rule. safer to edit policy to remove the variant pin.

jordan: if we unpin the rule, router will use regional preferences and avoid cross-region. do that.

<sara runs edit> ops-bot: Policy edit applied by sara: `route-by-cost-v2` -> removed variant pin for rule `enterprise-v2`.

support-bot: Metrics: error rate 14% -> 2.1% over 3min, latency stabilized.

maria (oncall): active customers reporting degradation reduced. support getting fewer tickets.

lee: note — when sara forced region, the forced queues bumped some DEDICATED pools above their autoscale thresholds, causing a slow scale-up and transient queuing. that's why we saw residual 502s. It wasn't a full outage, but customer-visible errors.

sara (oncall): lessons: don't force-region unless you validate pool headroom. I'll add a preflight script to `redwoodctl` for future forced overrides.

lia: also found a config drift: `redwood-13b-legacy` was removed from us-east during pruning but policy still referenced it. syncing the model catalog now. will push a fix to prevent stale variant pins.

jordan: creating an immediate alert for policy-config-version-mismatch and a short-term check in the rollout pipeline to validate variant availability before enabling pin rules.

maria (oncall): passing to infra to watch autoscale thresholds. i'll keep oncall until tomorrow 02:00 UTC as a precaution.

support-bot: Customer impact summary for SEV-2 ticket: ~150 customers experienced degraded responses (elevated 5xx/latency) for ~13 minutes. Major enterprise customers were impacted but no data loss.

lee: action items assigned: 1) lia - reconcile model catalog and block stale variant refs (PR ready). 2) jordan - add pipeline validation for pin rules (ticket #INC-2317). 3) sara - preflight for forced overrides (doc + script). 4) infra - tune autoscaler thresholds for forced bursts.

sara (oncall): thanks team. keeping this thread open for post-incident notes. tagging @oncall-next. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident transitioned to monitoring. Severity: SEV-2 -> Monitoring. Primary mitigations: policy unpin + forced-region (temporary).

lia: quick post-note — root cause: policy `route-by-cost-v2` contained a variant pin referencing a pruned model (`redwood-13b-legacy`) in us-east, causing cross-region fallback loops and KV cache churn. fix deployed.

jordan: will follow up with an RCA doc across eng-runtime and eng-platform. expected ETA for full RCA: EOD tomorrow.

sara (oncall): closing handoff to maria. leaving the thread.

maria (oncall): acknowledged, monitoring dashboards for 3 hours then will demote to normal ops.

support-bot: Closing customer-facing incident note draft: "Transient routing policy mismatch caused elevated errors for a subset of customers for ~13 minutes. Immediate mitigations applied and a permanent fix deployed. No customer data lost."

lee: adding one more note — avoid force-pin changes during regional pruning windows. will add to runbook.

sara (oncall): thanks everyone. good job moving fast and coordinating the handoff. :sparkles:
